summary:
Status: complete.

Summary: Reworked `.github/workflows/ci.yml` into two tiers and documented the tiers where CI is described. The sibling writer's mac gate work was read-only coordination — `release-binaries.yml` / `release.yml` untouched, so their build → test → package order is preserved.

What changed (worktree `/Users/sachinkoli/.hoocode/worktrees/noteapp/ci-tier`, branch `agent/ci-tier`, HEAD still base `4104d2b`, uncommitted):
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — dropped `cargo build --release --locked` from the test job (packaging workflows already build release; the release+dev double compile is gone). New `fast` job (ubuntu-only, all triggers): `cargo fmt --check` + `cargo check --locked --all-targets` + `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings` + `cargo test --locked -- --skip end_to_end` (skips the 22-chapter e2e session; verified the single `#[gpui::test]` entry point lives at path `shell::tests::end_to_end::end_to_end`). Existing `test` matrix (ubuntu+macos, single `cargo test --locked`, dev profile only) now gated to `main` pushes / nightly schedule (`17 3 * * *`, new) / manual dispatch, with `needs: fast`. Added `rustup component add rustfmt clippy` (the `minimal` profile omits them) and concurrency `ci-${{ github.ref }}` that cancels superseded runs except on `main`.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` — replaced stale "Linux, macOS and Windows" line with the tier description.
- `RELEASING.md` — replaced "CI runs on ubuntu-latest and macos-latest" with the tiered wording, noting the macOS leg still runs `cargo test` before packaging.

Verification:
- All 7 workflows YAML-parse: `ruby -ryaml` → `OK` on every file including edited `ci.yml`.
- No `run:` step in `ci.yml` compiles the crate more than once per profile — zero `cargo build` steps (one comment-only mention); `check`/`clippy`/`test` share the dev profile.
- Mac gate intact: matrix still `[ubuntu-latest, macos-latest]`, macOS leg's only test command is `cargo test --locked`.
- `git status --short` shows exactly 3 modified files; `git diff --stat`: `ci.yml 46 +++---`, `CONTRIBUTING.md 1`, `RELEASING.md 5`; nothing committed, branch never switched.

Estimated CI-minutes saved (reasoning, no live run available): per PR/develop push the old shape ran 2 full legs (release LTO build with `codegen-units=1` + dev test compile/run), including a macOS leg billed at 10×. The new shape runs 1 ubuntu fast leg with no release compile and no e2e — roughly 70–85% fewer billed minutes per feature-branch push (dominated by deleting the macOS leg and the release builds). On `main` the full matrix remains but each leg drops one full release compile (~30–40% wall-clock per leg given LTO/thin release builds dominate), plus fast-fails-first via `needs: fast` and PR-run cancellation via concurrency. Ranges assume release-profile compile ≥ dev test-compile time, which holds for this LTO/pinned-codegen profile.

Open questions:
- `--skip end_to_end` relies on the e2e test path containing that substring — true today (single entry `shell::tests::end_to_end::end_to_end`); if e2e is ever split into parallel tests the filter still matches by module path, but worth a comment check on future refactors.
- No live `gh workflow run` validation performed (sandbox); first merge to `main` should confirm the nightly cron and `if:` gating behave.
- Merge coordination: sibling's `release-binaries.yml`/`release.yml` mac-gate restore merges cleanly (different files, no overlap).
